name: DaVita Inc.
moat_justification: US dialysis duopoly (~38% share, ~72% combined with Fresenius), life-sustaining non-discretionary demand and scale, with ROIC proxy 11-20% over the last five fiscal years (17.9% in FY2025) — but the payer sets the price: Medicare/commercial reimbursement lags cost inflation (operating margin crushed to 11.5% in 2022), Fresenius is vertically integrated into equipment while DaVita buys from rivals, and GLP-1/transplant progress is a long-term volume headwind. Narrow moat, strong end.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 7.5%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 5.8x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier C (12.5%) vs bull-case tier A (20.9%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Durable dialysis duopoly, moat 6/10 — clears the 15% hurdle on the TTM base (17.4% weighted IRR, IV@15% $226.33 vs $187.31) but not on the 3-yr median base (14.6%, Tier C); sized to the conservative end it is a B, and it stops clearing 15% above ~$226.
moat_for: Duopoly scale: ~38% US share, 2,671 US centers, largest dialysis network
Life-sustaining, non-discretionary demand — patients cannot defer treatment; high switching friction via nephrologist relationships and clinic proximity
ROIC proxy above cost of capital through a cycle: 14.1% / 15.6% / 11.3% / 14.4% / 19.5% / 17.9% (FY2020-25, fundamentals.json)
Scale purchasing and clinical-operations leverage; Integrated Kidney Care extends the franchise into value-based care (~64,900 risk-based patients)
moat_against: No pricing power vs the payer: government reimbursement updates lag labor/cost inflation (FY2022 operating margin 11.5% vs 15.5% in FY2021)
Fresenius is vertically integrated (machines, NxStage home platform) and supplies equipment into DaVita's own home program; DaVita owns no equipment manufacturing
Commercial mix erosion: falling ACA exchange enrollment cuts the high-rate commercial share of revenue per treatment
Long-term volume risk from GLP-1 drugs slowing CKD progression and from transplant advances
Levered balance sheet (net debt $9.60B, 3.37x leverage) leaves little room for reimbursement shocks
